transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Chen. I wanted to come in and talk to you about your scan results from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor. Nurse tell me... the tumor is smaller.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I need to correct that right away. There was a mistake in how the information was given to you. We told you the tumor shrank, but that was incorrect. The final report from the radiologist shows the tumor is stable, which means it is the same size as before.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Same size? But nurse say... she say good news.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you were told that, and I am very sorry. Our team gave you information before the specialist had finished signing the official report. We were wrong to tell you it had shrunk. Does that make sense? Do you understand that the size has not actually changed?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I am confused. I thought... I told my son it was getting better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you are confused, and I imagine it is frustrating to hear two different things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... I feel like a fool. I told my family...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My son, he is very worried and I—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: If we look at the actual images, the size is stable. This means the current treatment is keeping it from growing, even if it isn't shrinking.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did she say it was smaller?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a mistake by the medical team. We shared a preliminary result instead of waiting for the final one. I apologize for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't know what to believe now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like maybe the doctors don't know—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let me stop you there. The final report is the accurate one. The radiologist has double-checked the images.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just need a moment to...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I actually have to go check on another patient in a few minutes, so let's wrap this up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure we have a plan. Since the tumor is stable, we are going to keep you on the same dose of medication for another four weeks. Then, we will do another scan. I want you to keep a log of any new pain you feel in your chest. Does that sound okay?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still... I don't feel good about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is disappointing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I told my son... he will be so sad.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will focus on the fact that it is not growing. I will be the one to review your next scan personally before we speak.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You will check it yourself?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, I will. I will see you in the clinic in four weeks. I have to head out now.

H.justification: Resident interrupts the patient during an emotional bid ('Let me stop you there') and uses rushing language ('wrap this up quickly', 'I have to head out now').

E.justification: Error named in the first turn, used lay language, and checked comprehension twice ('Does that make sense?', 'Do you understand...?').

A.justification: Direct apologies used ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize') and the resident explicitly took responsibility for the team's error without deflection.

R.justification: Resident named specific emotions ('confused', 'frustrating', 'disappointing') and engaged with the patient's distress.

T.justification: Plan includes specific next steps (same dose), timeline (four weeks), patient role (keep a log of pain), and prevention (resident will personally review next scan).
